# Munikajātaka (Ja 30)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Munikajātaka* (Ja 30) is a birth story belonging to the *Kuruṅgavagga* in the *Ekanipāta* of the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral]. The narrative was delivered by the Buddha at the Jetavana monastery regarding a monk who had become discontented after being seduced by a plump young woman (*thullakumārikā*), an incident noted as structurally linked to the *Culla-Nārada-Kassapa-jātaka* of the *Terasakanipāta* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the discontented monk in a past life was the pig named Munika (*Munikasūkara*), the young woman was the plump maiden, Cullalohita was Ānanda, and the Bodhisatta was Mahālohita [Fausböll 1877].

Neither SuttaCentral nor the DharmaNexus text-mining analysis identifies any Pali-internal passages or cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan for this discourse [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The Pali text and its commentary were edited by V. Fausböll in 1877, and modern translations listed on SuttaCentral include versions in four languages, notably an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral].
